title: Region eviction + GPU starvation drill with egress-silence dependency injection (automated fault runner)
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Objective: Validate graceful multi-region failover, circuit-breaker behavior, and load-shedding policies when faced with a simultaneous regional control-plane eviction and progressive GPU pool starvation while an external dependency (agent/process that provides metadata or telemetry, eg. feature-flag service or model shard indexer) enters an egress-silence state.

Hypothesis: With proper admission control, KV-cache priming, and prioritized routing, the platform will maintain error budget consumption below defined SLO thresholds (p99 latency and error-rate) by automatically diverting traffic, activating fallbacks, and shedding load without causing client-visible retry storms.

Scope: Full experiment will include three coordinated faults: 1) orchestrated region eviction (control-plane nodes removed, simulated networking partition for control plane only), 2) GPU pool progressive starvation (daemon that artificially reduces available GPUs in the pool across zones), and 3) dependency egress-silence (blackhole of outbound calls to the model-shard indexer / feature-flagger to simulate downstream dependency hang). The test will be executed against a shadow tenancy with synthetic traffic (mix of short-chat, long-completion, and embeddings) and ramped load to surface edge cases.

Out-of-scope: Stateful customer workload migrations, on-prem private deployments, and forced hardware failures (preemption) outside the simulated starvation logic.

Instrumentation and telemetry: Must capture and correlate the following signals: p50/p95/p99 latency per route, 5xx/4xx error rates, CPU/GPU utilization per instance, admission control rejections, queue lengths, KV cache hit/miss rates, retry counts per client, model-variant fallback invocations, and region-failover time to steady state. Dashboards: grafana/resilience/eng/eviction-drill (link in links).

Safety/rollback: Experiment runner respects a global kill-switch tied to on-call Slack alert; automatic abort if 5xx across prod-like synthetic traffic exceeds 3% for 3 continuous minutes or if any customer-facing region shows degraded SLOs. All steps will be gated by a manual approval in the Console and a runbook will be published to Confluence prior to the full run.

Automation: Implement the fault runner as a new submodule in chaos-runner (PR referenced below) with idempotent operations and dry-run capability. The runner will sequence faults with coordinated waits and injected observability (trace markers).

Deliverables: runbook, automation PR, grafana dashboards, postmortem checklist, and a guidance doc for engineers to translate run parameters to Dedicated customer contexts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Run automation in shadow tenancy without manual intervention (approve + kick).
- Failure detection and kill-switch validated in a canary mini-run.
- SLO pass criteria observed: synthetic traffic 99th latency increase < 2x baseline and end-to-end error rate < 1.5% during steady-state phase.
- Circuit-breakers trigger and routing fallbacks engage for >95% of failure cases.
- Post-run report with root cause mapping and list of mitigations and configuration changes.
- Runbook and automation merged and feature-flagged off by default.

2026-02-25: Safety criteria drafted; kill-switch integrated with on-call Slack channel. Lina to own runbook authoring.

2026-03-05: Mini canary executed against a single region with simulated GPU-starve; observed early admission rejections — adjusted admission throttle thresholds to reduce client retry amplification.
2026-03-09: Dependency-silence simulation added; noticed unexpected dependency caching behavior in model-shard-indexer fallback path. Added extra guard to avoid stale index reads.
